answer.text: Maintains shareholder records, processes transfers, corporate actions

explanation.text: The Logic: A Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) is the SEBI-regulated record-keeper appointed by an issuer or mutual fund to maintain investor/shareholder records, process transfers and transmissions of securities, effect changes such as address and bank-account updates, and execute corporate actions like dividend payouts, bonus issues, and rights entitlements. The RTA acts as the operational interface between issuers and investors. The Trap: Brokers execute trades on exchanges — that is a separate intermediary role. Issuers (companies/governments), not RTAs, issue bonds. Exchanges and market participants set prices — RTAs do not. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (Sep 2025) lists RTAs among market intermediaries on pages 39-41 and mentions RTA fees for effecting transfers on page 155, but does not specifically describe maintaining shareholder records and processing corporate actions as the RTA's role on the cited pages. The framing above is general SEBI-intermediary-framework knowledge.
